title: ESAF Small Finance Bank Ltd - 544020 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Credit-led recovery at a microfinance-heavy SFB: Q4 PAT only INR 24 crore, GNPA 5.4% and credit cost 1.08% in the quarter, with management guiding to 2% steady-state credit cost by FY28.

summary.headline: ESAF SFB Q4 FY26 PAT rose to INR 24 crore from INR 7 crore in Q3; GNPA fell to 5.4% and NIM rose to 7.3%.
summary.overview: Total business reached INR 48,276 crore at March 2026, up 15% YoY, with gross advances up 19% and deposits up 11%. Q4 FY26 net interest income was INR 518 crore versus INR 432 crore in the prior quarter, and pre-provisioning operating profit rose 166% YoY to INR 241 crore. Asset quality improved: GNPA fell to 5.4% from 6.9% and NNPA to 1.8% from 3.0% YoY, with Q4 slippages of INR 106 crore versus INR 427 crore a year earlier. Management framed FY26 as two halves, with the second half showing improvement from secured-asset mix shift, collections and cost discipline. Management guided to steady-state credit cost of about 2% from FY28, steady-state ROA of 2%, and NIM of about 7%, while noting provisioning backlog will persist in FY27.

segments.name: MARG (MSME, Agriculture, Retail, Gold)
segments.commentary: MARG advances grew 47% YoY, with gold and mortgage loans each up over 50%; MARG disbursements grew 133% in FY26. Secured share of advances rose to 61% from 53%.

segments.name: Microfinance
segments.commentary: Microfinance book stable at INR 8,746 crore at March 2026; its share of gross advances fell to 39% from 47% a year earlier. Management is taking a calibrated, risk-averse approach.

segments.name: Disbursements
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements were INR 12,926 crore, up 88% YoY and broadly flat QoQ; FY26 disbursements were a record INR 42,530 crore, up 103%. Secured share was 78% in Q4 and 82% for the full year.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Retail deposits were 92% of total deposits versus 93% last year; 88% of bulk deposits carry a non-prepayment clause.

guidance_outlook: Secured assets target of 70% by March 2027; management said it is on track. On the call, the unsecured book glide path was corrected to about 30%, not 20%.
Steady-state loan growth of 20% to 25%, excluding INR 650 crore of books offloaded via IBPC in FY26.
Cost-to-income ratio of about 55%, plus or minus 2%.
NIM at steady state of about 7%, plus or minus 0.5 percentage point; NII has almost reached steady state.
Credit cost of about 2% at steady state from FY28, with provisioning backlog continuing through FY27; steady-state ROA target of 2%, with traction expected over the next couple of quarters.
ESAF 2.0 (StratoNeXt) core technology programme expected to complete before Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Distribution footprint of 804 banking outlets, 720 ATMs, 1,047 customer service centres and 32 institutional business correspondents across 24 states and 2 union territories.
ESAF 2.0 – StratoNeXt digital transformation to be completed before Q3 FY27, targeting core infrastructure, data governance and risk management.
Crossed 10 million customers during the year, with strong representation of women borrowers.
demand_pricing: Q4 disbursements grew 88% YoY, with secured lending at 78% of disbursements, the sixth straight quarter above 75%.
Management said no ARC sales or technical write-offs occurred in Q4, and that Sangam process changes, graduation to individual lending and delinquency resolution are underway in microfinance.
Management described the microfinance industry as stabilising, with collection efficiencies improving, though geopolitical developments remain a watchpoint.

qa_highlights.question: Given the shift to secured lending, what normalised credit cost is expected and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 credit cost was 1.08%, including provisioning backlog on existing NPAs. Steady-state credit cost of about 2% is expected from FY28, with backlog provisioning continuing through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state ROA is expected with the MARG focus, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is planning for an ROA of 2%, targeted by FY28. Traction is expected within a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What loan growth trajectory should be expected after the lean two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state growth of 20% to 25% is the target; FY26 growth excludes INR 650 crore of IBPC book offloads.

qa_highlights.question: Will NII grow in line with the loan book?
qa_highlights.answer: NII has reached a steady state; NIM of about 7%, plus or minus 0.5 percentage point, is the expected going-forward level.

risks_watch: Provisioning backlog on existing NPAs will keep credit cost elevated in FY27 before the 2% steady state in FY28.
Management's FY27 growth and ROA outlook was not given numerically; the 2% ROA target is for FY28.
CASA ratio is low at 23.9%; management expects gradual improvement but gave no target.
Geopolitical developments are a stated watchpoint for the microfinance sector recovery.
Q4 PAT of INR 24 crore is small in absolute terms; ROA of 0.1% and ROE of 1.3% are non-annualised.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously confident: management highlights sequential improvement in asset quality, margins and profitability, but repeatedly ties recovery to a stabilising external environment. On forward targets such as FY27 growth and ROA, it was vague, declining to give numbers.
key_quotes: Gireesh C. P.: Yes, NII, has almost reached to a steady-state basis. So somewhere around 7 %, plus or minus half percentage will be the NIM going forward.

Gireesh C. P.: It is a futuristic statement and I'm unable to give you at this moment. But one thing which I can tell is that the growth is back and the asset quality problems are almost over and going forward we will be on a steady kind of growth.

growth.why: Management guides steady-state loan growth of 20-25% (ex INR 650 crore IBPC offloads), NIM about 7%, cost-to-income about 55%, and 2% credit cost and 2% ROA from FY28; backing is partial, citing secured mix shift (70% target by Mar 2027, on track), disbursements up 88% YoY in Q4, and cost discipline, with no specific capacity additions disclosed.
